calls.head: Nowhere to hide for DeBrincat
calls.body: At home, the Lightning keep sending Mikheyev’s line (Mikheyev, Girgensons and Holmberg) out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Jon Cooper has been giving this group the hard job of facing the other team’s top line. Tonight the Red Wings’ first line is DeBrincat, Finnie and Kasper.
calls.call: The Lightning’s L2 (Mikheyev, Girgensons and Holmberg) spends at least 57% of its 5-on-5 time against the Red Wings’ first line, against about 46% with no line matching.
calls.nums: At home: 68% of this group’s 5-on-5 time against first lines, about 46% with no line matching

chips.tip: Tampa Bay’s L2 (Mikheyev, Girgensons and Holmberg) at home: 68% of its 5-on-5 time against opponents’ first lines. Matchups, Tampa Bay home games this season, 8 games, 72 minutes for this group at 5-on-5.
With no line matching, this group would face first lines about 46% of the time, about as often as those lines are on the ice.

calls.happened: Tampa Bay’s L2 (Mikheyev, Girgensons, Holmberg) spent 24% of its 5-on-5 time against Detroit’s L1 (3:42 of 15:25). The call needed 57%, halfway from the 46% it would get with no line matching to its home habit of 68%.

lane.tip: Share of this group’s 5-on-5 time against that line tonight (the filled dot). The ring is the call: halfway from what it would get with no line matching (the tick) to its home habit (the dotted mark), since part of any habit is luck. Reaching the ring holds the call; past the tick is partly; otherwise it didn’t happen.

calls.title: Mikheyev, Girgensons and Holmberg barely saw the Red Wings’ first line
calls.plain: Tampa Bay sent Mikheyev, Girgensons and Holmberg out against the Red Wings’ first line no more than they would with no line matching. Instead, Cooper sent them out against Brandsegg-Nygård, Copp and Raymond (10:39 of 15:25 at 5-on-5).
calls.said: Jon Cooper would send Mikheyev, Girgensons and Holmberg out against the Red Wings’ first line again

calls.head: Tilted ice, toward the Red Wings’ net
calls.body: At 5-on-5, the Lightning have been one of the league’s best at getting more of the chances than they give up, and the Red Wings around the middle. The ice should tilt the Lightning’s way, even if goaltending and bounces have the final say on the score.

TBL.head: We gave Tampa Bay a 64% chance, but Detroit had other ideas.

DET.head: We gave Detroit only a 36% chance, and they proved us wrong.

surprises.head: Daniil Tarasov stole one with a shutout
surprises.body: Tarasov stopped all 31 shots, worth 2.9 expected goals. That is more than Detroit’s winning margin, not counting empty-net goals. Starting goalies have a night this good about once every 60 starts.

story.head: Nothing gets past Tarasov
paras: Lucas Raymond opened the scoring for the Red Wings midway through the second, and Michael Brandsegg-Nygård sealed it into the empty net with 43 seconds left.

The Lightning had the better of the chances. Replay those chances a hundred times and the Lightning win about seven in ten. Daniil Tarasov made the difference in net, stopping 31 of 31. Andrei Vasilevskiy stopped 20 of 21 for the Bolts.

Only two penalties were called all night, something the league sees about once every 20 games. The Red Wings improved to 8-10-3 and climbed off the bottom of the Atlantic to seventh, while the Lightning dropped to 13-5-2, still first in the Atlantic.

items.text: The Red Wings won for the first time in six games.
The Red Wings’ Andrew Copp played his 800th NHL game and had an assist.
NHL.com had projected the Lightning with 12 forwards and six defensemen, but they dressed 11 and seven.
The season series is even at 1-1.
